source_caption:
🎬 Furry Vengeance (2010)

Furry Vengeance follows Dan Sanders, a hardworking real estate developer who moves his wife and teenage son from Chicago to a peaceful community in Oregon to oversee the construction of a new residential development. Hoping the project will provide a better future for his family, Dan quickly discovers that his demanding boss has ambitious plans to transform the surrounding forest into a massive commercial development. However, the local wildlife has absolutely no intention of allowing its natural habitat to be destroyed. Led by a clever raccoon, a determined group of forest animals begins launching an outrageous campaign to sabotage Dan’s work and drive him away. From mischievous squirrels and angry birds to skunks, bears, and other woodland creatures, the animals use increasingly creative tricks to turn Dan’s everyday life into complete chaos. As their hilarious attacks escalate, Dan struggles to convince his family and coworkers that the animals are deliberately targeting him. Meanwhile, his relationship with his son becomes strained as the family begins questioning the environmental consequences of the development project. Through embarrassing accidents, chaotic confrontations, and unexpected lessons, Dan gradually realizes that protecting nature may be more important than completing his assignment. Combining slapstick comedy, family-friendly adventures, and an environmental message, Furry Vengeance explores family, responsibility, conservation, teamwork, and the importance of respecting the natural world.

🎭 Genre: Comedy • Family

⭐ IMDb: 3.9/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 32m • PG

🎥 Director: Roger Kumble

✍️ Writers: Michael Carnes & Josh Gilbert

source_details.synopsis: Furry Vengeance is a 2010 family comedy film directed by Roger Kumble and written by Michael Carnes and Josh Gilbert. It stars Brendan Fraser, Brooke Shields, and Ken Jeong. The film tells the story of a real estate developer charged with changing a forest into a residential community, which evokes the wrath of local forest animals. Furry Vengeance was theatrically released on April 30, 2010, by Summit Entertainment. The film was a box-office disappointment, earning $39 million on a $35 million budget, and received generally negative reviews from critics.
